segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I, then, the prisoner in the Lord, urge you to walk in a way worthy of the calling with which you were called,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: making every effort to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One body and one Spirit, just as you were also called in the one hope of your calling;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: one Lord, one faith, one baptism;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But to each one of us grace was given according to the measure of Christ’s gift.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Therefore it says:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “When he ascended on high, he took captives captive; he gave gifts to people.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now what does “he ascended” mean, if not that he also descended to the lower regions of the earth?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The one who descended is himself also the one who ascended far above all the heavens, so that he might fill all things.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And it was he who gave some as apostles, some as prophets, some as evangelists, some as shepherds and teachers,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: to equip the holy ones for the work of service, for the building up of the body of Christ,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: until we all come to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a full-grown man, to the measure of the stature of Christ’s fullness,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so that we may no longer be infants, tossed by the waves and carried about by every wind of teaching, through the trickery of people, through cunning that serves the scheming of error,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but rather, speaking the truth in love, may grow up in every way into him who is the head, Christ,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: from whom the whole body, joined and held together through every supporting ligament, as each single part does its work in due measure, brings about the body’s growth, so that it builds itself up in love.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So I say this and insist on it in the Lord: you must no longer walk as the Gentiles walk, in the futility of their minds,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: being darkened in their understanding, alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance that is in them, because of the hardening of their hearts.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They have lost all feeling and have given themselves over to debauchery, for the practice of every kind of impurity, with greed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But that is not how you learned Christ,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: if indeed you heard him and were taught in him, just as truth is in Jesus,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: that you are to lay aside the old person who belongs to your former way of life and is being corrupted through the desires that come from deceit,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: to be made new in the spirit of your mind,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and to put on the new person, created in God’s likeness in the righteousness and holiness that come from truth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Therefore, laying aside falsehood, speak the truth, each of you with your neighbor, because we are members of one another.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Be angry and do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and do not give room to the devil.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Whoever steals must steal no longer, but must rather labor, doing what is good with their own hands, so as to have something to share with anyone in need.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Let no rotten word come out of your mouth, but only what is good for building up where there is need, so that it may give grace to those who hear.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Let all bitterness and rage and anger and shouting and slander be removed from you, along with all malice.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Be kind to one another, compassionate, forgiving each other just as God in Christ also forgave you.

notes.note: Older translations have “meekness,” which now suggests weakness or timidity. The Greek word describes someone who is not harsh or self-assertive, without any implication of weakness. “Gentleness” or “humility” is the mainstream modern rendering.

The quotation is from Psalm 68:18 (67:19 in the Septuagint). Both the Hebrew and the Septuagint say that the victor “received gifts among people,” whereas the wording here says he “gave” them; a similar reading appears in the later Aramaic paraphrase of the Psalms, and scholars debate whether the author follows an existing interpretive tradition or adapts the text to his point. The introductory “it says” could also be translated “he says,” with God as the speaker.

notes.phrase: the lower regions of the earth
notes.traditional: the lower parts of the earth
notes.note: The phrase can mean the regions beneath the earth, that is, the realm of the dead, or “the lower regions, namely the earth,” in which case the descent is Christ’s coming into the world. Both readings have strong scholarly support, and a minority takes the descent as the giving of the Spirit after the ascension. The translation leaves the phrase as open as the Greek. Some manuscripts add “first” after “descended.”

The Greek word is the ordinary one for a shepherd, used as a picture of those who look after a community. “Pastor” is the Latin word for shepherd but now names a church office, and this is the one place where most translations use it instead of “shepherds.” Because “shepherds and teachers” share a single article in Greek, many scholars think one group, or two closely overlapping groups, is meant.

“Saints” now suggests canonised individuals or people of exceptional virtue. The Greek word is used of all members of the community as people set apart for God, echoing the Septuagint’s language for Israel. Many translations keep “saints”; others use “God’s people.”

notes.traditional: for the work of the ministry
notes.note: The three phrases of this verse can be read as parallel, so that the leaders are given for equipping, for ministry and for building up. Here, as in most modern translations, they are read in sequence: the leaders equip all the holy ones, who then do the work of service. The Greek word covers service of many kinds, from waiting at table to carrying out a commission, whereas “ministry” now suggests clergy.

The Greek uses the word for an adult male with an adjective meaning complete or fully grown, in contrast to the “infants” of the next verse. The whole community is pictured as a single person growing to adulthood. Older versions have “a perfect man”; many modern ones paraphrase as “maturity” or “mature manhood.”

The verb can mean telling the truth or, more broadly, being truthful and holding to what is true in conduct as well as speech. Most translations have “speaking the truth,” which fits the contrast with deceitful teaching in the previous verse. Some scholars prefer “living the truth” or “being truthful.”

The Greek word means “nations” or “peoples.” In the plural it is the regular Jewish term for the non-Jewish peoples, and this translation renders the one word as “Gentiles” or “nations” according to sense. The readers were themselves of non-Jewish origin (2:11), so the word here points to the way of life of peoples who do not know God.

The three infinitives in verses 22–24 (lay aside, be made new, put on) give the content of what the readers were taught. They can be read as instructions still to be carried out, as here, or as statements of what happened at conversion (“that you have laid aside the old person”). The parallel in Colossians 3:9–10 speaks of it as already done. The image is of taking off and putting on clothing.

notes.traditional: the old man; the old self
notes.note: The Greek word means a human being, not specifically a male, and not quite “self” in the modern psychological sense. The phrase denotes the person one was before, seen as a whole way of being human. Some scholars take it corporately, of the old humanity as against the new humanity created in Christ (compare 2:15).

Greek has a single word-family where English has two (righteous/just, righteousness/justice), so “righteousness” here covers doing what is right and just. “Holiness” translates a word different from the usual one for “holy”; it denotes devotion to God, and the pair was a common Greek way of summing up right conduct toward people and toward God. “That come from truth” answers “that come from deceit” in verse 22; many translations instead render “true righteousness and holiness.”

notes.phrase: Be angry and do not sin
notes.traditional: Be ye angry, and sin not
notes.note: The words reproduce the Septuagint of Psalm 4:4 (4:5 in its numbering). Most interpreters take the imperative not as a command to be angry but as a concession: when you are angry, do not let it lead to sin. Verse 31 goes on to say that anger is to be removed altogether.

candidates.reason: The Semitic idiom of “walking” for conduct recurs throughout Paul and John, and translators split between “walk” and “live,” so one policy is needed.
A central term across the New Testament whose senses (grace, favor, gift, benefit, thanks) need a governed split so that the English does not vary arbitrarily.
“Ministry” versus “service” (and “deacon/servant/minister” for the cognates) varies widely between translations and affects how readers picture church roles.
Rendered “pastors” only here in the tradition but “shepherd” everywhere else; a single decision would keep the image consistent with John 10, Hebrews 13:20 and 1 Peter 2:25.

candidates.rendering: the old person / the new person
candidates.reason: The “old/new man” phrase recurs in Romans 6:6, Ephesians 2:15 and Colossians 3:9–10, and “man,” “self,” “person” and “humanity” are all in use.
